$comment: P69 L2 (lane lm; the review of checkpoint 29, its MINOR finding 11 and BLOCKERs 1 and 2): a constant condition's TYPE decides its value, and the lowering marks what follows an `if` never reached when it folds the condition true or false — so a fold that types a constant wrongly kills the program at run time. Every `if` here is folded (each operand a constant) and is taken both ways across the program: a statement expression's value and a bit-field promoted by its width (A), a conditional balanced by its arms with an unselected `1 / 0` (B), a float conditional and a float chain rounded at float (C), `__builtin_types_compatible_p` as an `int` (D), a `const` array read whole as its address (E). MEASURED 2026-10-20 on checkpoint 29's bytes, one cell per check (probes/l2): C's float conditional stopped the compiler (exit -6), D and E died of an illegal instruction (pe64 0xc000001d, ELF SIGILL) and C's chain folded 1 where C gives 0; clang 18.1.3 and gcc 13.3.0 build THIS file at -std=gnu2x and -std=gnu17, -O0 and -O2, and exit 42 (each warns `z == 0` / `!z` always false / true). The TYPE of `({ g.b; })` is a fork (gcc promotes it, clang and DSS keep the declared type), so A asks its value only. Exit 42, or the number of the first check that fails. The release arm folds the same conditions through the optimizer.
